correctness.rationale: Expanding g(x+u) conjugate(g(x)) into chirp/chirp, chirp/indicator, indicator/chirp and indicator/indicator yields p zeta^(au^2) on v=2au plus 2k+C_u prime-root summands with nonnegative integer coefficients. For prime p, a vanishing p-root sum must have equal exponent counts, so p must divide the total number of summands, congruent to L_u modulo p even on the chirp line. With 0=L_u^(-(p-2)); on line triangle inequality gives p-L_u>=1. Weyl characters diagonalize the Hermitian-matrix lifting, yielding sqrt(p)|A| singular values, with ||g||^2<=p+3k. Independently reconstructed residue counts for p=5,7,11 all supports k
residual_risks: Prime p and exactly +1 real impulses essential; the 1/3 fraction is sufficient, not necessary or asymptotically optimal; algebraic lower bound may be very conservative.

value.rationale: An all-position adversarial construction of full Gabor phase retrieval from a natural quadratic chirp, tolerating a positive fraction of perturbed entries, is a substantive stability/design question. The explicit overlap-sensitive modular certificate explains which support geometry matters and produces exact boundary cancellation witnesses; it is not merely a renamed k=1 identity. Quantitative if conservative singular-value control makes the result useful for robust finite tomography.
residual_risks: No claim that one-third is optimal or that fewer Gabor measurements suffice; a future sharper margin remains open.

final_claim: For every odd prime p>=5, nonzero quadratic coefficient a and arbitrary nonempty support U of size k with 3k<p, adding unit indicators at U leaves all p^2 self-ambiguity coefficients nonzero; the stronger sufficient modular test is p not dividing 2k+|U cap (U-u)| for all u. A concrete Galois-norm singular-value bound and three exact failures beyond the sufficient density are given.
limitations: Prime p and exactly +1 real impulses essential; the 1/3 fraction is sufficient, not necessary or asymptotically optimal; algebraic lower bound may be very conservative.
A more general theorem on sparse positive perturbations of perfect sequences or cyclotomic phase masks could imply the multi-impulse guarantee; historical priority not certified.
Novelty excludes the previously known k=1 case and the generic Gabor nonvanishing criterion.
